Hey /v/linuxgaming,

To preface, I am primarily a Windows user/developer, but I have been using Ubuntu and I'm really taking to it. I've created a game that will be on Steam and I am supporting (the best I can) a Linux build and I'm looking to increase my knowledge of Linux as a whole.

My particular question has to do with Linux distributions. I use a number of libraries for my game. All of the libraries build and work fine when in Ubuntu (which I'm targeting), but when I try to build for Debian, the repo is missing some dependancies.

I know different distros have different repo contents, but is something like this common among distros? Do Linux gamers more or less expect developers to support as many distros as possible, or is it "par for the course" for them to target one specific distro? I definitely have gaps of knowledge here and I'm looking for some insight.

Thanks.
Question to Linux Developers/Gamers About Distributions

Yes, this is common. Each distro has their own package management ideology. Distros like Arch or Gentoo will have the latest, most bleeding edge code but Debian and even Ubuntu to a point, rely on stable code. The best thing to do is to build it against Steam's runtime. That way, as long as the user has Steam installed, it doesn't matter what distro they are using.

While it is much appreciated that you try to support as many distros as possible out of the box, I would also reccomend you publish a list of libraries you use, so there is some point for gamers to start if something does not work. Often times, it is quite easy to get a specific library if you just know which one you need, but sometimes it is difficult to figure out which libraries a game expects to find. I personally don't mind getting a couple of packages myself if the game just clearly tells me what it needs to run. So documentation is key, as always ;).
